messages.body_plain:
Hi Michael,

[2014-07-31 23:49] Michael Friendly wrote:
> I'm setting up a new Win 7 64-bit machine, with eclipse/StatET for
> all my R package development work.
>
> Two quick questions:
>
> - My last install was eclipse 3.8 on a laptop, where everything worked
> fine with StatET / svn / R-Forge.  Is the current version of StatET
> from the download site fully compatible with eclipse Standard 4.3.2
> (Kepler), or should I go with a previous version like 4.2.2 (Juno)?

At moment I recommend version Eclipse 4.3.2 or 4.4.0.

>
> - I installed the HD from my old computer with my workspace files,
> now at D:\Documents\workspace, containing all my R projects, .svn,
> etc.  Is is safe to simply use this as the workspace on my new computer
> or is it more prudent to re-create the workspace de novo, by creating
> new R projects, Importing from svn/R-Forge, etc. ?

You can usually simply reuse the complete workspace.

I you prefer to use a clean workspace resetting all Eclipse preferences, 
you can still reuse your project directories:
   - Make sure you have a backup of your workspace
   - Remove the .metadata directory from your workspace
   - Start Eclipse and use the import wizard (menu: File > Import...)
     "Existing Projects into Workspace" to import your projects.

Regards,
Stephan


>
> best & thanks,
> -Michael

Dear all,

    I have two questions regarding the use of the "object browser" and
"Variables" view while debugging.

1) When I am debugging a function (i.e., by setting a breakpoint or a
"browser" instance within a function), I don't seem to be able to access
the "values" of the variables defined within the function through the
object browser. The only variables I can see are that of globalenv. Is it
supposed to work like this, or am I missing something ?

2) I know I can use the "variables" view while in debugging mode to see the
variable vallues. However, I noticed that when I stop within a function
which I called with several parameters, the "variables" view doesn't show
the "values" of the variables I passed, but only their name, and the
"actual type" column shows "promise".
Stepping through the code with F6 I saw  I get  the "values" to show in the
variables window only after the "passed variables" are somehow "used" in
the code, even if I am sure they are already defined. Similar problems
happen if I inspect the variables by "hovering" on them : I see for
example  something like "language  symbol reproj", instead of the values of
"reproj".

Is this a bug, or am I missing something ?

Thanks in advance for any help,

Lorenzo

messages.body_plain:
Hi Lorenzo,

The "Object Browser" shows the list of attached packages and R objects 
comparable to the R function "search". The "Variables" view shows the 
frames of the call stack comparable to the R function "sys.frames".

If an R object is shown as "promise" element, it is a promise object not 
yet evaluated in R. In R, for example function arguments are evaluated 
lazily and so they appear as promise elements in the Variables view. It 
is a feature, not a bug: if StatET would directly evaluate all promise 
objects, it would run the risk of changing the behaviour of your code 
and the result of your function.
You can simply force the evaluation e.g. by printing the argument in the 
console.

Regards,
Stephan
